history.summary: POSSIBLE DUPLICATE of seq 640 ('ISKCON Temple Imphal' — same temple). ISKCON was first established in Manipur on 25 December 1977 at Thakurbari, Paona Bazar, Imphal, under His Holiness Bhaktisvarupa Damodara Swami (Dr. T.D. Singh, founding director of the Bhaktivedanta Institute), on the instruction of his spiritual master A.C. Bhaktivedanta Swami Prabhupada. It later moved (via rented premises at Paona Bazar) to Sangaiprou, where the temple was established in 1980. The centrepiece is the Sri Sri Radha Krishnachandra Manimandir: an elegant white-coated brick structure with a distinctive dome, Krishna-pastime murals, carved-wood interior and a naturally lit sankirtan hall. It is a major Gaudiya Vaishnavite centre of northeast India with daily aratis, kirtans and Gita/Bhagavata discourses.

name: ISKCON Temple, Imphal
town_description: Imphal is the capital of Manipur, set in the flat Imphal Valley at about 786 m and ringed by hills. It is the historic seat of the Meitei kings — Kangla Fort, the former royal palace and the Govindajee temple stand at its centre — and the heart of Manipuri Vaishnavite culture, classical dance and handloom. The city is Manipur's road and air hub, served by Bir Tikendrajit International Airport and national highways to Nagaland, Assam and Myanmar.
